scenes.kicker: A software factory, shown end to end
scenes.title: Idea to Value
scenes.say: How an idea written in an issue becomes a reviewed, tested change, with people deciding only where it matters.

scenes.title: A factory, for software
scenes.define: A written route that every piece of work follows. Agents do each stop the same way every time, scripts check the result, and people approve at the gates.
scenes.explain: A software factory is a written route that every piece of work follows. Agents do each stop the same way every time, scripts check the result, and people approve at the gates. It turns “ask an assistant to write some code” into a process you can repeat, inspect and trust.

scenes.title: Six words to know
points: The stops a piece of work passes through, in order.
One job. Done by an agent, or by a script.
How a stop is done, written down once.
Where the work waits for a person to approve.
Proof that a stop passed its checks.
Picks up new work and keeps it moving.
scenes.explain: Six words describe the whole thing.

scenes.title: One factory, many repositories
points: One editor and one background job, on one machine.
As many as you like. This demo uses two: an API and a UI.
Each repository has one or more: features, bugs, reviewing pull requests.
scenes.explain: There is one factory: one editor and one background job. It serves as many repositories as you like, and each repository has one or more routes, such as a route for features, a shorter one for bugs, and one that reviews pull requests. This demo runs five routes across two repositories. One limit to know: a single route works on one repository, so an idea that spans two is two issues today.

scenes.title: Set up the factory, once
scenes.say: Three steps. After this, the factory is running and waiting for work.
scenes.explain: Three steps, done once per machine. After this the factory is running and waiting for work.

scenes.title: Get the factory
scenes.say: Clone it. It needs Python, Claude Code, and a login to your tracker.
Clone it, and check the three things it needs

scenes.title: Open the editor
scenes.say: Everything from here is done on a page, not in files.
One command opens the editor in your browser

scenes.title: Start the background job
scenes.say: It checks for new work every ten minutes. Nobody has to start anything again.
Install the job once. It keeps running.

scenes.title: Give a repository its route
scenes.say: Six steps in the editor. Here: a route for feature work on the UI repository.
scenes.explain: Six steps in the editor. These frames show a real route being created: feature work on the UI repository.

scenes.title: Add a repository
scenes.say: Tell the factory where the code is and give the route a name.
The editor lists every route in the factory. Add one.
Name the route and point it at the code

scenes.title: Pick a starting point
scenes.say: Start from an example and edit it, or from nothing. Examples are not fixed types.
Examples to start from. Any kind of work can have a route.
The route exists and is listed in the factory

scenes.title: Say what triggers it
scenes.say: Which repository, which label, and who the issue must be assigned to.
Only issues with this label, assigned to this person, are picked up

scenes.title: Arrange the stops and gates
scenes.say: The stops are the work. The gates are where a person approves.
This route has two gates and ends with a pull request
Each stop is a row: reorder it, switch it off, or add your own

scenes.title: Write the rules
scenes.say: The team's rules in plain words, and the commands that prove a change works.
Agents read these rules before every task

scenes.title: Switch it on
scenes.say: From here the background job watches this repository.
Switch on automatic pickup, and save

scenes.title: From idea to value
scenes.say: One idea, written as an issue, taken all the way to a pull request. A person decides twice.
scenes.explain: One idea, written as an issue, taken all the way to a pull request. A person decided twice; everything else was done by agents and checked by scripts. It took about 16 minutes.

scenes.title: Write the idea down
scenes.say: An issue in the tracker, in plain words, with the label and the assignee.
The idea, as a person wrote it

scenes.title: The factory picks it up
scenes.say: Nobody starts it. The background job finds the issue on its next pass.
The Activity page: the factory is already running
The issue is on the line and an agent is at work

scenes.title: Approve the requirements
scenes.say: The route stops at its first gate. A person reads, then decides.
Waiting for you: the route has stopped
Read what the agent wrote before approving
Approve. The optional stop is skipped for a small change.

scenes.title: Agents build, scripts prove
scenes.say: A maker builds each task. A checker verifies it. A script re-runs the checks.
Building, with nobody at the keyboard
The work is split into tasks, and every task names its skill
Evidence: what was expected, and what was found
The factory's log: scripts verify before the route moves on

scenes.title: Look at the result, and approve
scenes.say: The second gate is for a person to look at what was built.
The board before
After: built from that one issue
The detail the issue asked for is there
A person approves the second gate

scenes.title: Ready to merge
scenes.say: The route ends with a pull request. Merging it is a person's decision, and that is where the idea becomes value.
Every stop done, and a pull request open
The pull request, with the spec and the evidence attached

scenes.title: Other routes, same factory
scenes.say: A bug needs a shorter route. An API change needs a stricter one.
scenes.explain: The same factory runs other routes at the same time. On the API repository, feature work has two gates before any code, because API changes are costly to undo. Bugs take a short route with no spec: reproduce with a failing test, fix, review, then one gate. A bug filed in this demo went from issue to a reviewed fix in under three minutes.

scenes.say: API features: requirements and design are both approved before any code
A bug route: picked up in the background like any other
Reproduced, fixed and reviewed in under three minutes
And its pull request, opened after one approval

scenes.title: No process, no review
scenes.say: Every pull request is checked by a script first. Only work that followed the process earns an agent's time.
scenes.explain: A review route checks pull requests, whoever wrote them. A script goes first: is there a spec, does every task name a skill, is there evidence, did the tests change with the code, plus the team's own rules. A quick hack added by hand was stopped by the script and cost nothing. The request the factory built passed all 11 checks, and only then did an agent review the code.
scenes.how: Label a pull request factory-review. Set the rules in the editor's Review rules tab.

scenes.say: A quick hack with no spec and no test: stopped by the script
The request the factory built passes every check
Only then does an agent review the code
You decide how strict each check is
And add your own rules by filling in a sentence

scenes.title: Four ideas in, four pull requests out
scenes.say: 7 gates approved by a person. Everything else was done by agents and checked by scripts. Agent cost for all of it: $13.04.
scenes.explain: Across two repositories and five routes, four issues became four open pull requests, each with a spec or a reproduction, evidence, and passing tests. A person approved seven gates and will decide what to merge.
